content:
maria: Heads-up — canary rollout of kernel switch (v2->v3) now showing intermittent OOMs and a 12-18% p99 token latency blip. KV cache hit-rate looks fine, but fragmentation reported on GPU workspace. attaching quick flame snapshot and perf counters in a sec

ben: saw that too on a handful of requests. not consistent, seems correlated with mixed-length batches hitting the prefill path then falling back to decode-only.

kai: can you drop the perf output? curious if memcpy vs kernel time shifted after swap.

maria: pasted perf summary:
```
# perf-summary
total_samples: 100000
kernel_memcpy: 41.2%
runtime_attention: 29.5%
kv_prefill_path: 14.0%
allocator_lock: 6.8%
decoder_step_kernel: 4.5%
```
Looks like memcpy and allocator_lock went up after kernel change.

anika: interesting — increased memcpy could indicate less buffer aliasing or smaller contiguous slabs after alloc changes. frag increases cause more small allocs -> memcpy churn.

ben: replicated locally with synthetic traffic (mix of 32/512 tokens). profiler shows many small KV allocations on prefill path: lots of ~8-16KB slices. those are killing the slab packing efficiency.

sam: `infra-bot` ran an oom-dump:
```
OOM at workspace_alloc: requested 9.2MB, free largest 6.1MB
stack: workspace_alloc -> allocate_slab -> memcpy -> kernel_launch
```
We should avoid returning OOMs by soft-capping per-request prefill.

kai: proposal: introduce two quick knobs and test canary:
- per_request_prefill_cap (tokens -> kv slots) default 8
- slab_compaction_trigger_pct default 18% (when fragmentation > pct trigger compaction pass)
This reduces small alloc churn and forces reuse before making new tiny allocations.

maria: + add metric: prefills_blocked_by_cap and compaction_runs. want visibility before/after.

ben: also surfaced a batching heuristic opportunity — if batch contains both short and long sequences, route short ones to decode-path (no prefill) when batch size < threshold to avoid mixed hot-paths. simple rule: if median_len < 64 and any len > 256 then split.

anika: love that. it avoids expensive prefill for mostly-short groups. but keep a fallback: if latency SLO allows, prefill may still be better for quality. we should gate by route config.

maria: ran an A/B locally: enabling per_request_prefill_cap=6 dropped allocator_lock samples by 55% and memcpy by 30%, p99 token latency back to baseline. KV hit-rate dropped ~1.8% but end-to-end quality unchanged for our eval set.

ben: did you try slab_compaction_trigger_pct=15?

maria: yeah, compaction reduced fragmentation (largest_free raised) but compaction itself costs ~3-5ms when it runs; with compaction threshold tuned it amortizes well.

kai: next steps I'd suggest for canary rollout:
- add metrics (prefills_blocked, prefills_routed_to_decode, compaction_runs)
- run 50% canary with per_request_prefill_cap=6 and batching split rule for mixed-length batches
- keep compaction trigger conservative (18%) and monitor compaction_gc_time histogram
- enable temporary verbose allocator logging for canary to capture rare edgecases

maria: +1. Also add a small guard: if request.is_dedicated (Dedicated pools) we keep cap higher (12) — customers on Dedicated expect throughput over micro-optimizations.

sam: putting the rollout in the deployment tracker: `deploy-tool rollout --service=runtime --canary=0.5 --env=canary --cfg=allocator_prefill_cap=6,batch_split=true,compaction_pct=18`

infra-bot: deploy job queued: job_id=J-98321. will report results to #eng-runtime-canary once finished :rocket:

ben: one more thing — kernel selection path needs a small tweak: when we pick v3 kernel it should check current fragmentation metric and prefer v2 for high-frag hosts until compaction runs. this avoids oscillation.

anika: agree. add hysteresis: prefer v2 if frag > 22% and only switch back after two consecutive checks < 12%.

maria: logging note for the canary: include `allocator_frag_pct` and `vm_largest_free` in the trace event for every request so we can correlate per-request latency with frag.

kai: nice. once we have data, we'll iterate on the cap and compaction threshold. good progress. :thumbsup:

ben: filing a short follow-up doc with the perf screenshots and the exact perf commands I used. will link here when ready.

maria: thanks all — I'll kick off the rollout and post first-hour metrics snapshot here.
